title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized lookups (e.g., Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id), RuleSnooze.objects.get_or_create(...)). No raw SQL or string interpolation into queries is used.

The `rule_id` comes directly from the URL path parameter and is used to fetch both `Rule` and `AlertRule` objects without verifying they belong to the requested `project`. An attacker could supply a `rule_id` from a different project/organization and snooze a rule they should not have access to. The `ProjectEndpoint` base class validates project membership but does not ensure the fetched rule is scoped to that project.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the lookups to the project or organization, e.g.: `Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id, project=project)` and `AlertRule.objects.get(id=rule_id, organization=project.organization)` to ensure the rule belongs to the authorized project.
